passage:
Monday: Tejas saw Hrithik narrow his eyes at him across the classroom. He's angry about the cricket match, Tejas thought, and stayed away from him all break.
Wednesday: Hrithik narrowed his eyes again, first at Tejas, then at the board. Tejas noticed the sun glaring on the board through the window. “Are you okay?” he whispered. “I can't read with that glare,” said Hrithik.
Friday: Sir moved Hrithik's seat, and Tejas saved him a place at cricket.

qa.q: Where was the sun glaring on Wednesday?
qa.a: The sun was glaring on the board through the window.

qa.q: What did Tejas think on Monday when Hrithik narrowed his eyes, and how reliable was that reading?
qa.a: He thought Hrithik was angry about the cricket match. It was only a guess, as Wednesday showed that the narrowing could come from glare.

qa.q: What could Tejas do differently from Monday?
qa.a: Check the context first, such as the light and whether Hrithik can see, or ask kindly, as he did on Wednesday.

qa.q: How might Hrithik have felt when Tejas stayed away on Monday?
qa.a: Confused or left out, since he probably did not know why Tejas was avoiding him.

grounding: A child reads a classmate's narrowed eyes as anger, but it was squinting at glare.

passage:
“Listen, Arohi,” said Kamal Mama, “when I was your age, my friend Sunil squinted hard at me during a cricket match. I decided he was cross about a catch I dropped. I stayed away from him for a week. Then I saw him squinting at the scoreboard, at the road signs, at everything far away. He needed spectacles, that's all! Nothing to do with me.” He shook his head. “Now I look at the light and whether the person can see before I decide anything. Or I ask.”
“And Sunil?”
“He was hurt I'd gone quiet.”

qa.q: How long did Kamal Mama stay away from Sunil?
qa.a: He stayed away for a week.

qa.q: What did Kamal Mama first think Sunil's squint meant, and what did he later realise?
qa.a: He first thought Sunil was cross about a dropped catch. Later he saw Sunil squinting at everything far away and realised it was about seeing.

qa.q: What would you advise Arohi to do when someone squints at her?
qa.a: Look at the light and whether the person can see well, and ask kindly before deciding they are angry.

qa.q: How might Sunil have felt when Kamal went quiet?
qa.a: Confused and hurt, since Kamal says he was hurt that Kamal had gone quiet. He had probably done nothing wrong.

grounding: A child misreads a squint as anger; checking the context avoids unfair conclusions.
